question: Does the independently confirmed source-predicted monotone neutral base produce a visibly better fixed-AO6 result than the global monotone neutral base when compared blind against the same target look?

comparison.reference: confirmation filtered target followed by unchanged AO6
comparison.candidate_global: confirmation source followed by frozen global monotone curve, analytical safety and unchanged AO6
comparison.candidate_ridge: confirmation source followed by frozen source-predicted monotone curve, analytical safety and unchanged AO6
comparison.criterion: prefer the candidate closer to reference tone and colour while rejecting any candidate with a confirmed severe artifact

selection.method: sort all 64 rows by signed ridge-minus-global neutral RMSE, split into four contiguous equal strata, take indices 1,5,9,13 within each stratum, then sort pair_id before each round permutation

branch_rules.pass: retain source-predicted monotone curves as the preferred optional auto-base before fixed AO6 and open runtime/profile compilation work without film or stock claims
branch_rules.fail: keep the simpler global curve or current global AO6 path; do not tune the curve predictor or blind set

assessment_label: autonomous blinded visual target-match evidence; not human population preference
claim_ceiling: blind visual product-value evidence for one explicit digital neutral base before fixed AO6; not film, stock, calibration, owner preference or product promotion
